question.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $C$ to the basis $B$ is given by
${P}_{C\to B}=[\begin{aligned}-6 & -5 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}].$ Find the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$  .
question.worked_solution:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is the inverse of the change-of-coordinates matrix from $C$ to $B.$ Therefore, we simply need to find the inverse of the given matrix.

Computing the inverse of ${P}_{C\to B}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{B\to C} & ={P}_{C\to B}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}-6 & -5 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-6)\cdot 4-(-5)\cdot 5}[\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ -5 & -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =1\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ -5 & -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ -5 & -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
